sec-oncall-bot: ALERT: EDR detected suspicious outbound connection from macbook-alex-23 (user: alex.k) -> 45.33.12.9:443. Confidence: high. Action taken: file quarantined (~/Downloads/runner_updater.dmg), process terminated. Hash: sha256:ab12...ef34
alex.k: Uh — I just saw my laptop CPU spike and a popup. I didn't click anything weird today.
rachel: Oncall, can you isolate the device from network (quarantine at edge) and revoke any active session tokens for alex.k?
sec-oncall-bot: Isolation requested. Applied host isolation policy "host-isolate-network" for macbook-alex-23. Time: 1979991130.
maria: I'm running a quick triage script now, will paste output. 
4BB alex.k: Thanks. I'm standing by.
ken: Can we get the process tree and the quarantine filename? Need to know if this attempted SSH key exfil or plain HTTPS.
sec-oncall-bot: Quarantined file: /Users/alex/Downloads/runner_updater.dmg, process: /usr/bin/curl -> /private/tmp/installd. EDR rule: macos-suspicious-dmg-download (v7).
sre-team: Blocking outbound IP 45.33.12.9 at egress ACLs now. ETA 2m.
maria: Paste of quick triage (sanitized):
```
=== macbook-alex-23 triage ===
User: alex.k
Process list (relevant):  1978 curl  -> 2021 installd
Open sockets: 45.33.12.9:443 ESTABLISHED
Loaded kernel extensions: none suspicious
SSH keys in ~/.ssh: unchanged
Recent log excerpt: Nov 12 10:12:02 installd[2021]: extracting payload
Nov 12 10:12:03 installd[2021]: spawning postinstall script: /private/tmp/.updater.sh
```
ken: That postinstall script is suspicious. Can you cat /private/tmp/.updater.sh (if it's safe) and upload to the stash?
maria: Uploaded the script to /tmp/artifacts/1979991111_updater_sh.txt (sha256:cd34...aa98). Script looks like downloader + base64 blob decode -> write to ~/.cache/.svc -> chmod + launchd plist.
rachel: Ok escalate: assume credential access attempt. Rotate any AWS keys used from dev laptop CI? Alex, do you have any AWS CLI profiles on this machine?
alex.k: I use a personal profile for home projects but not company creds. I do have a cached gcloud token for a personal project. No company AWS keys on this laptop.
ken: Check ~/.ssh/authorized_keys and known_hosts? Also check ssh-agent output.
maria: ssh-agent dump: only local keys, no agent forwarding detected. ~/.ssh shows only personal keys; no new files were created under ~/.ssh during timeframe.
sec-oncall-bot: Incident ticket created: #INC-2024-4123 (link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2024-4123). Assigned: eng-security, priority: P2.
rachel: Maria, please run a full AV + EDR deep scan + YARA match across user profile. Also export EDR full event JSON and attach to ticket.
maria: Running deeper scan now. ETA 12m.
sre-team: Egress block confirmed for 45.33.12.9 across all regions at 1979991168.
it-support: Alex, recommend we issue a new company laptop image for you to work on until we finish. Want to ship replacement or remote wipe?
alex.k: Prefer remote wipe and new image, please — I need to keep working.
it-support: Roger. Scheduling remote wipe and replacement checkout.
ken: Two quick checks for later: 1) KMS CMK usage logs for any decrypt calls from alex.k principal in the timeframe. 2) Audit logs in IAM and session tokens rotated?
rachel: Good call. @eng-infra can you check CloudTrail for any suspicious KMS/Decrypt or PutObject calls from that source IP or alex's principal between 1979991100-1979991200?
sre-team: Also flagging any burst of token introspection or service account usage.
eng-infra: Looking now. Initial CloudTrail query: no KMS Decrypt events from alex.k principal in range. There are two PutObject attempts to an internal s3-bucket from a different service account at 1979991125, unrelated. Will expand query.
maria: Deep scan results: EDR full-scan found dropped payload and launchd plist in ~/Library/LaunchAgents/.svc.updater.plist, quarantined. No sign of private keys exfiltrated. YARA matches: downloader_stub pattern.
ken: Upload sample to malware-sandbox for detonation (low-risk VM). Once we have network indicators, search SIEM for lateral attempts.
sec-oncall-bot: Malware sample uploaded to sandbox queue. Job ID 98765.
rachel: For comms: post incident note to #incidents with summary once we have sample verdict. Keep external comms minimal.
alex.k: Appreciate the quick responses everyone. I'll hand over laptop to IT for remote wipe.
it-support: Remote wipe scheduled for 1979991250, replacement delivery queued.
maria: Sandbox verdict: downloader creates second-stage encrypted payload which attempts to POST to 3 different endpoints; no immediate C2 beacon after 24h sandbox run. Indicators: 45.33.12.9, 104.248.58.22, 198.51.100.44.
ken: Ok next steps: 1) Full employee token rotation for alex.k (done) 2) Re-image laptop and confirm secure baseline (IT doing) 3) Search endpoint fleet for LaunchAgent pattern "svc.updater.plist" and the base64 blobs. 4) Add detection rule for downloader_stub v7.
rachel: Adding follow-up tasks to INC-2024-4123, tagging eng-ml for potential model-data exposure check (just in case).
maria: Fleet-wide search: 1 hit on macbook-ops-01 (non-prod), quarantined remotely. No other hits.
sre-team: No suspicious service traffic observed from infra networks.
sec-oncall-bot: Incident status: Contained. Host isolated, sample quarantined, egress blocked, token rotations started. Updated priority to P3.
ken: Post-incident action items: timeline, detection gap analysis (how did downloader bypass prior heuristics), add KMS audit alert for any Decrypts by user principals, improved endpoint posture for DMG installer files.
rachel: I'll schedule a 30-min postmortem tomorrow 11:00 with eng-security, eng-infra, IT, and SRE.
alex.k: Thanks all. If you need my input for timeline I'll be available.
sec-oncall-bot: Thread closed to edits at 1979991375."
